liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Highlights traditional music influence in this song, In the Pines, and Sitting on Top of the World [5]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (1 review): Describes this song as awesome, with the live music sounding better than their first album [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.21063.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 101 min; rated 4.69/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Describes the audio as having a bubble gum feel, like a 60s Haight Ashbury documentary; Notes the vocal track is panned left, while the music track is panned differently [8][10]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.89555.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 101 min; rated 4.09/5 by 22 [2]. Said about its sound: States the sound is pristine despite the recording being almost 43 years old at the time [12]
- **gd1966-07-16.13958.serafin-marmar-sbefix-4459.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 44 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.serafin.4459.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 44 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [4]

## Around the show

- Recalls LSD was legal earlier that year, with Bear home-brewing and European labs shipping quantities [14]
- Listener recalls being 15 and getting hooked on the music after a friend played the tape [15]
- Claims this show has an edge over the November 19, 1966 performance due to its fantastic sound [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.21063.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.89555.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD [2]. Also: Listener thanks Mr. Gans and Mr. Miller for the archival transfer of the recording [7]
- **gd1966-07-16.13958.serafin-marmar-sbefix-4459.flac16**: transferred by sbefix etc of source by Marmar; source: SBD > RTR > PCM > SSSB [3]. Also: Mr. Marmar processed files in December 2002 using shntool to correct sector boundary errors [3]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.serafin.4459.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by John "Jay" Serafin; source: SBD > RTR [4]
